desc:
Given an integer array nums, count the index quadruples a < b < c < d with nums[a] + nums[b] + nums[c] = nums[d].

Quadruples are distinguished by position, so equal values at different positions count separately. Return the count modulo 1,000,000,007.

For example, nums = [1, 2, 3, 6] gives 1, nums = [3, 3, 6, 4, 5] gives 0, and nums = [1, 1, 1, 3, 5] gives 4.
hints: Four nested loops are O(n<sup>4</sup>), and the standard optimisation to O(n<sup>3</sup>) is still too slow for 700 elements. Rewrite the equation to split it into two pairs.
nums[a] + nums[b] = nums[d] - nums[c]. The left side is a sum of the pair (a, b), the right side a difference of the pair (c, d), with b < c separating them.

Sweep b from right to left. Keep a hash map of all differences nums[d] - nums[c] with c > b and d > c. For each a < b add map[nums[a] + nums[b]] to the answer. Before moving b one step left, insert the pairs whose c is the old b.
editorial: Move nums[c] to the right side: nums[a] + nums[b] = nums[d] - nums[c]. Now the left pair (a, b) and the right pair (c, d) are independent except for the ordering b < c, which we enforce with a sweep over b from n - 3 down to 1.

Maintain diff[v], the number of pairs (c, d) with c > b, d > c and nums[d] - nums[c] = v. When the sweep arrives at a new b, add the pairs with c = b + 1 (one per later d) to the map; then every a < b contributes diff[nums[a] + nums[b]]. Each pair of positions is inserted once and queried once, so time and space are O(n2). The count can reach C(700, 4), about 1010, so reduce modulo 1,000,000,007.
